item.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Board Vote
item.description:
Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Board Vote

Nvidia announced on Monday morning that the board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following discussions and meetings with Huang. The board stated it was satisfied with Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. The board also confirmed that it received input from senior levels of the United States government and determined that Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk. Donald Trump responded on Truth Social, stating that Nvidia made the correct decision and that the U.S. government has no reason to believe Huang’s return poses any risk to national security, citing the Attorney General’s confirmation that no evidence of unlawful conduct exists.

📋 Key facts

  • The board voted unanimously to bring back Huang as CEO, President, and Board director
  • The board received input from senior levels of the United States government
  • The investigation into reports of a Chinese spy plot will continue with Huang’s support
  • Interim CEO Colette Kress will remain as CFO
  • Harvey Jones will remain as board chair
  • Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports of extramarital affairs
  • More than 200,000 people, including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, Garry Tan, and Travis Kalanick, signed a letter calling for his reinstatement
  • Nvidia shares tumbled in Huang’s absence
  • Industry analysts expressed concerns about an outsider replacing him
  • The board maintained as recently as last Tuesday that Huang wasn’t coming back

🗣️ Statements

  • Huang said: “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.”
  • Huang added: “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.”

🇺🇸 Government perspective

  • The U.S. government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security
  • The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct

🔁 Leadership structure

  • Colette Kress – Interim CEO (will remain as CFO)
  • Harvey Jones – Board chair (will remain in role)

#Nvidia #JensenHuang #CEO #USGovernment #NationalSecurity

Source: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO

item.title: Jensen Huang Rumored to Seek CEO Return Amid Ongoing Nvidia Leadership Drama
item.description:
Jensen Huang Rumored to Seek CEO Return Amid Ongoing Nvidia Leadership Drama

The leadership drama surrounding Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly as rumors suggest he is seeking a path back to his former position. While some high-profile tech figures advocate for his reinstatement, others point to allegations of workplace misconduct as a significant barrier to his return.

🔍 Overview

Jensen Huang has reportedly discussed the possibility of returning as CEO with close allies. This development comes as some Silicon Valley insiders and employees attempt to pressure the Nvidia board to reinstate him. However, the situation remains complicated by the circumstances of his departure and recent statements from related firms.

⚙️ Key details

A public campaign to reinstate the former CEO has gained significant traction, though the validity of its support is under scrutiny.

  • Public Letter: A letter calling for Huang to be reinstated has over 150,000 signatures.
  • High-Profile Support: Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have publicly thrown their support behind the demand to “bring Jensen back.”
  • Verification Issues: Business Insider reports that the signature list includes likely fake names such as “Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor” and “Xi Jingping,” which appears to be a misspelling of the Chinese president.

💡 Why it matters

The debate over Huang’s return has sparked a wider conversation about power and accountability in Silicon Valley.

  • Conduct Allegations: According to the Financial Times, one ally acknowledged that having an affair with a subordinate is a “fireable offense.”
  • Industry Criticism: Many women in Silicon Valley see the situation as an example of leveraging power to pursue sexual relationships with employees.
  • Cultural Impact: 23andMe founder Anne Wojcicki told Bloomberg that “power corrupts” and that people may act as if they are “untouchable” when they are treated like gods.

🧩 Organizational Status

Recent statements have clarified the current status of individuals involved in the ongoing controversy.

Person Role/Status Details
Jensen Huang Former CEO Rumored to be plotting a return and discussing the possibility with allies.
Alice Huang Former Employee Megaspeed claims she left the company effective Aug. 30, 2025, and currently has no role there.

#Nvidia #JensenHuang #SiliconValley #CorporateGovernance
